# ToolBox4Devs — Full Technical Specification for AI Agents & Crawlers

Website: https://www.toolbox4devs.com
Architecture: 100% Client-Side React SPA / Static SSG
Data Transmission: 0 bytes outbound (all operations run in browser memory)
Pricing: 100% Free Open Source & Ad-Free
Total Tools: 77

## Tool Registry & Technical Specifications (All 77 Tools)

### 1. .env File Auditor & Secret Detector
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/env-auditor
- Category: Analyze (analyze-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Compare .env and .env.example files, detect missing or duplicate keys, catch leaked API secrets, and generate sanitized templates.
- Summary: .env File Auditor & Secret Detector parses .env and .env.example files entirely inside your browser to surface missing environment variables, undocumented keys, duplicate definitions, empty values, and accidental secret leaks (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Stripe, Slack, JWTs, PEM keys, and database URLs with credentials).
- Use Cases: Verifying that local .env files contain every required variable defined in .env.example before deploying; Scanning .env.example files before a git commit to ensure no real API keys or database passwords slipped in; Detecting duplicate dotenv keys that silently override earlier lines; Generating an alphabetically sorted, secret-free .env.example template from an existing .env file
- Features: Side-by-side .env vs .env.example key comparison (missing, undocumented, and empty keys); Built-in pattern & Shannon entropy detector for AWS, GitHub, OpenAI/Anthropic, Stripe, Slack, Google, JWT, and PEM secrets; Masked secret previews so sensitive tokens are never echoed in full inside findings; Duplicate key line-number reporting matching dotenv override semantics; One-click generator for sorted .env and sanitized .env.example templates
- Tip: Paste your .env into the left panel and leave .env.example empty to automatically generate a clean, sorted .env.example template with all values stripped.

Featuring 12+ pre-installed procedural templates across geometries, materials, animations, and product showcases, it provides a live WebGL 2 rendering environment with PBR studio lighting, camera controls, and zero external network calls.

- Features: 12+ pre-installed procedural 3D templates across 4 specialized categories; Live WebGL 2 rendering with ACESFilmicToneMapping and SRGB color space; Interactive code editor with instant execution and error feedback; OrbitControls camera movement and RoomEnvironment studio reflections

### 3. DevFlow Pipeline Studio
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/pipeline-studio
- Category: Analyze (analyze-tools)
- Complexity: Advanced
- Description: Visual developer workflow pipeline to chain, format, decode, filter, and hash payloads in zero-latency browser memory.
- Summary: DevFlow Pipeline Studio connects multiple client-side developer transformations into a continuous, zero-latency visual execution chain. Decode Base64 strings, beautify JSON, extract nested keys, inspect JWT claims, run regex replacements, and generate SHA-256 hashes sequentially without switching tabs or copying across tools. 100% private in browser memory.
- Use Cases: Chaining multi-step decoding: Base64 decode to formatted JSON to key extraction; Unpacking nested webhook and API authentication tokens without leaving your browser; Cleaning and deduplicating massive server logs with regex filters and sorting; Converting API model properties from camelCase to SQL-compliant snake_case; Sharing reproducible developer debugging pipelines with teammates via compressed URL hashes
- Features: Visual sequential step pipeline with real-time execution timing in milliseconds; Reorder, enable, disable, and configure parameters on any transformation step; Pre-built curated developer recipes for webhooks, auth tokens, logs, and database naming; One-click URL hash sharing with zero server roundtrips using compressed state; Intermediate step inspection and live final output diffing; 100% Client-Side execution — zero outbound network requests or server telemetry
- Tip: Need to share a complex transformation chain with a teammate? Click "Share Recipe" to generate a self-contained compressed URL that restores your exact input and steps.

### 4. Delimited File Data Validator (CSV / TSV / TXT)
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/csv-validator
- Category: Data (data-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Validate CSV, TSV, and delimited TXT files against custom column schema rules, required fields, data types, regex, and unique checks with row-level error reporting.
- Summary: The Delimited File Data Validator enables developers and data engineers to verify structured CSV, TSV, and text files against customizable column rules (data types, required values, numeric/date ranges, regex patterns, enum lists, and uniqueness) completely in-browser without uploading data to external servers.
- Use Cases: Verifying bulk ETL files and database import dumps before ingestion; Checking user registration CSV exports for missing required values or malformed emails; Auditing pipe-separated or comma-separated supplier data feeds for allowed status codes; Isolating and exporting invalid rows for remediation workflows
- Features: Support for CSV, TSV, pipe-delimited (|), and semicolon-delimited text files; Interactive visual rule builder with auto-inference from sample records; Rule checks: Required (not empty), Types (String, Integer, Number, Boolean, Email, UUID, Date), Min/Max, Regex, Enum, and Uniqueness; Row-level error explorer with category filters, live search, and full record inspection modal; Export options: Error Audit CSV, Invalid Rows Only CSV, and Valid Clean Rows CSV; Export and import column validation rules as standard JSON schemas; 100% private in-browser memory execution with zero telemetry or network calls
- Tip: Click "Auto-Infer Rules" after loading your data to automatically generate base rules, then fine-tune required and regex constraints.

### 6. JSON Formatter & Validator
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/json-formatter
- Category: JSON (json-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Status: Beta
- Description: Format, validate, query, filter, repair, and inspect JSON in real time with non-blocking Web Worker performance. 100% client-side.
- Summary: JSON Formatter & Validator instantly formats raw or minified JSON into clean, readable output with proper indentation. Powered by an asynchronous non-blocking engine, it supports massive JSON payloads, JSONPath & JS expression filtering, interactive collapsible Tree & Table visualizers, 1-click Auto-Repair for broken JSON, key case conversions, and TypeScript interface exports. Everything runs in your browser, no data is sent anywhere.
- Use Cases: Formatting minified API responses into readable, indented JSON; Filtering large JSON responses with JSONPath, dot notation, or JS expressions; Fixing relaxed or broken JSON (unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas, Python literals); Inspecting deep JSON hierarchies with an interactive Tree Explorer and Table Grid; Validating JSON payloads with pinpoint line & column syntax error diagnostics; Generating TypeScript interfaces and type definitions directly from JSON; Minifying JSON payloads to reduce bandwidth and payload size for production
- Features: Non-blocking background processing supporting large multi-megabyte JSON files; Format with 2 spaces, 4 spaces, 3 spaces, or Tab indentation, plus minification; Pinpoint syntax error locator with visual indicator and 1-click Auto-Repair; JSONPath, dot notation, and JavaScript expression query filter engine; Interactive Collapsible Tree Explorer with type highlighting and quick JSONPath copy; Searchable and sortable Table Grid view for JSON arrays with instant CSV export; Deep structural metrics: key counts, nesting depth, type breakdown, and compression analysis; Key sorting (A-Z, Z-A, Natural, Length) and recursive key case conversions; Export to TypeScript interfaces, YAML, or downloadable JSON file; 100% Client-Side execution — zero data sent to external servers
- Tip: Need to extract specific data from a nested API response? Use the Query bar with dot notation like "data.products[*].name" or a JavaScript expression like "x => x.price > 100" to filter instantly.

### 24. HMAC Generator & Calculator
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/hmac-generator
- Category: Crypto (crypto-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Calculate HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, and HMAC-SHA1 signatures for webhook verification and API security.
- Summary: HMAC Generator & Calculator computes Keyed-Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) signatures using Web Crypto standard algorithms including SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384, and SHA-1. It supports Hex, Base64, and Base64URL output encodings and UTF-8, Hex, or Base64 secret keys.
- Use Cases: Testing and validating GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, and Razorpay webhook payload signatures; Debugging REST API request signing mechanisms (e.g., AWS V4 signatures or custom API headers); Verifying message integrity between distributed microservices; Generating sample Node.js and Python verification code for backend handlers
- Features: Supports SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384, and SHA-1 hash algorithms; Flexible secret key encodings: Plain Text (UTF-8), Hexadecimal, and Base64; Multiple output formats: Lowercase Hex, Uppercase Hex, Base64, and URL-safe Base64URL; Pre-built preset configurations for Stripe, GitHub, and Shopify webhooks; 100% Client-Side Web Crypto API execution — your secret keys never leave your device
- Tip: For GitHub webhooks, choose HMAC-SHA256 with Hex (lowercase) output format to match the X-Hub-Signature-256 header!

### 62. Base32 Encoder / Decoder
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/base32
- Category: Encode / Decode (encode-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Encode text to RFC 4648 Base32 or decode Base32 back to text, with optional padding.
- Summary: Base32 encodes bytes using the 32 characters A–Z and 2–7, defined in RFC 4648. It is case-insensitive and avoids characters that are easy to confuse, which is why it is used for TOTP secrets in authenticator apps and in some identifiers. This tool encodes UTF-8 text to Base32 and decodes Base32 back to text in your browser.
- Use Cases: Reading the text behind a Base32 string from a config file or API; Encoding a test value for code that expects RFC 4648 Base32; Checking whether a string is valid Base32 before using it; Comparing padded and unpadded Base32 output
- Features: Encode UTF-8 text to standard RFC 4648 Base32; Decode Base32 back to UTF-8 text; Optional "=" padding when encoding; Decoding accepts lower case, spaces and missing padding; Clear errors for invalid characters, misplaced padding and impossible lengths; Swap the output back into the input to convert the other way
- Tip: Like Base64, Base32 is an encoding, not encryption. Anyone can decode it.

- Features: Configurable delimiter styles: standard colon (00:1A:2B), hyphen (00-1A-2B), and Cisco dot (001a.2b3c.4d5e); Custom uppercase or lowercase hexadecimal casing; Bulk generation with one-click copy and list download; 100% in-browser generation with zero network requests
- Tip: Use Cisco dot notation (xxxx.xxxx.xxxx) when provisioning Cisco IOS and network switch configurations.

### 74. Password Strength Analyzer
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/password-strength-analyzer
- Category: Analyze (analyze-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Analyze password entropy, estimate crack times, detect common patterns, and get actionable improvement tips — all in your browser.
- Summary: Password Strength Analyzer evaluates the security of any password by calculating information entropy (in bits), estimating crack times across online, offline, and GPU-accelerated attack scenarios, detecting common patterns and sequential characters, and providing actionable improvement suggestions. Everything runs locally in your browser — no password is ever transmitted.
- Use Cases: Auditing password strength before deploying a new application; Teaching users about password security and entropy; Evaluating passwords generated by password managers; Testing password policies and complexity requirements; Demonstrating the impact of character diversity on security
- Features: Information entropy calculation in bits using character pool analysis; Crack time estimates for online (~100/s), offline (~100K/s), and GPU (~10B/s) attacks; Common password pattern detection (dictionary words, sequences, repetitions); Character set breakdown (lowercase, uppercase, digits, special characters); Visual strength meter with score out of 100; Actionable improvement suggestions based on detected weaknesses; Copyable analysis report for documentation and compliance
- Tip: A strong password uses 12+ characters with a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters — and avoids common dictionary words or patterns like "Password1!"

### 77. X.509 Certificate Decoder & Inspector
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/certificate-decoder
- Category: Crypto (crypto-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Decode and inspect PEM SSL/TLS X.509 certificates, SANs, validity dates, and fingerprints privately.
- Summary: The X.509 Certificate Decoder parses and inspects PEM-formatted SSL/TLS certificates completely inside browser memory using WebCrypto and a client-side ASN.1 parser. Inspect Common Names (CN), Organizations, Subject Alternative Names (SANs), validity periods, public key algorithms, and SHA-256 fingerprints with zero network calls.
- Use Cases: Inspecting SSL/TLS certificate validity windows and remaining days before expiration; Checking Subject Alternative Names (SANs) to verify domain and subdomain coverage; Verifying certificate issuers, Distinguished Names, and intermediate CA chains; Generating SHA-256 and SHA-1 certificate fingerprints for pinning and validation
- Features: Decodes standard PEM format X.509 certificates (SSL/TLS, CSR, and CA); Validity countdown with days remaining and expired/not-yet-valid status flags; Detailed Subject and Issuer Distinguished Name extraction (CN, O, OU, C, ST, L); Subject Alternative Name (SAN) DNS and IP address extraction; Public key type (RSA bit length, ECDSA curves) and signature algorithm identification; Live SHA-256 and SHA-1 cryptographic fingerprint calculation via WebCrypto; 100% private and runs locally — certificates and keys never leave your machine
- Tip: Paste certificates directly from your server configuration or click "Let's Encrypt TLS Cert" to test instantly.

## Developer Workflow Recipes
- Hub URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes
- Description: Pre-assembled sequential multi-tool pipelines executing client-side with zero latency.
- Recipes:
  1. Webhook Payload Inspector (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/webhook-payload-inspector): Extract, decode base64 bodies, and prettify webhook payloads from Stripe, GitHub, or Shopify entirely in browser memory.
  2. JWT Auth Token Inspector (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/jwt-auth-verifier): Extract claims from Bearer authentication tokens, validate expiration timestamps, and generate SHA-256 fingerprints in local browser memory.
  3. Base64 JSON Unpacker (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/base64-json-unpacker): Decode base64 and url-safe base64 strings directly into clean, syntax-highlighted, formatted JSON in a single step.
  4. Log Cleaner & Deduplicator (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/server-log-cleaner): Extract error lines, deduplicate stack trace signatures, and clean messy server log files in browser memory.
  5. SQL Identifier Sanitizer (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/sql-identifier-sanitizer): Batch transform frontend camelCase models and JSON keys into Postgres and MySQL compliant snake_case identifiers.
